thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered for P1: cachebridge-eu connection errors impacting auth-cache (source: cache layer metrics)

Jun (SRE): seeing 5xx spike on auth-cache reads, rate limiter firing, 503s cascading to API. Graphs show Redis connection errors from CacheBridge EU region.
Marta (Platform): confirmed, span: cachebridge.eu.* connection_errors up 420% since 08:12 UTC.
Caroline (Support): multiple customer tickets about slow auth + 502s, highest impact on enterprise customers in EU.
Ryan (Eng-Infra): drop-in logs from the pool:```
ERR: Failed to GET key user:auth:token - dial tcp 10.2.3.4:6379: connection reset by peer
ERR: pool exhausted - no connections available
```
Jun (SRE): mitigation plan: 1) route reads to local LRU fallback for non-critical keys, 2) broaden rate-limiter token bucket to allow grace for auth checks, 3) failover to secondary cache provider for writes that can tolerate eventual consistency.
Marta (Platform): can we flip read-fallback gate? it's behind feature-flag `cache_fallback_local`.
Ryan (Eng-Infra): I can flip it now. Doing: `curl -XPOST https://config.internal/flags/cache_fallback_local -d '{"enabled":true}'` -> (200) enabled.
Caroline (Support): putting a short note to affected customers: "We are experiencing degraded auth lookups in EU due to our cache provider. We have enabled local fallbacks and are working on a permanent fix. No credential compromise."
Jun (SRE): rolling throttle update: increasing per-customer token refill from 10r/s -> 20r/s for auth route to reduce bursts causing connection saturation. Command:```
infractl ratelimit update --route=/v1/auth --refill=20 --burst=40 --env=prod-eu
```
deploy-bot: Rate-limit config change applied in 3s, rollout to all pods.
Ryan (Eng-Infra): starting an outbound failover to backup cache provider (cachebridge-fallback) for non-urgent writes. Executing playbook step: `./scripts/swap-cache-target --target=cachebridge-fallback --scope=auth-cache --mode=gradual`
Marta (Platform): enabling KV prefix caching for auth tokens to reduce cache trips: `redis_local_cache.enable_prefix('auth:')` -> enabled.
Jun (SRE): impact assessment: internal metrics show auth latency median from 45ms -> 280ms at peak; error rate for /v1/auth jumped to 7.2% (baseline <0.1%). Top affected customers: AcmeCorp, FathomAnalytics, and BetaPay (EU). Noted in incident board.
Caroline (Support): I pushed an update to status.redwo od.com: "Degraded performance in EU for auth checks. Mitigations in progress." (link: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/CB-2026-03-15)
Jun (SRE): short-term mitigations working: errors down to 1.1% post-fallback, median latency 120ms. Still seeing occasional spikes when batch jobs run.
Marta (Platform): added temporary circuit-breaker on large batches from our ingestion pipeline to prevent pool exhaustion. Policy: `reject if concurrent > 50`
Ryan (Eng-Infra): cachebridge support responded: they are investigating a connection pool leak in their EU cluster and will attempt rolling restart of a subset of pods. ETA 30-45m.
Jun (SRE): good. Plan for next 60m: keep local fallback enabled, keep rate-limiter relaxed, maintain backup provider for writes, monitor error budget. If CacheBridge doesn't recover in 45m, we escalate to account AM and prepare full written customer comms.
Caroline (Support): queued a customer-facing email template for enterprise customers; include workarounds: short-lived token refresh or login retry.
Jun (SRE): handoff checklist for next on-call: 1) current mitigations and flags (cache_fallback_local=true, auth-rate-refill=20), 2) monitor dashboards: auth-errors-eu, cache-connections, rate-limit-drop, 3) open actions: follow up with CacheBridge ticket #CB-6423, coordinate cross-region traffic if needed, draft postmortem owner. I'll assign postmortem to Ryan.
Ryan (Eng-Infra): I accept postmortem. Will start timeline collection after incident.
incident-bot: Note: Pager cleared for Jun (SRE) at 09:12 UTC but escalation continues.
Jun (SRE): handing off to Ryan for the next 2 hours. Summary: partial recovery, provider is restarting; keep fallbacks live, don't revert flags until provider confirms stable for 30m.
Ryan (Eng-Infra): taking over. I'll keep the channel updated every 15m.
Caroline (Support): reopening tickets if replication issues persist. Will attach workaround steps to each.
Jun (SRE): final note before handoff: collect heap/dial metrics for cache clients (agent logs saved at s3://redwood-logs/incidents/1799943210/).
Ryan (Eng-Infra): got it. Starting metrics scrape.

(reacts: :thumbsup: from Marta, :eyes: from Caroline)

Jun (SRE): Post-incident action items (brief):
- Run client-side connection pool audit and harden retry/backoff (owner: Ryan)
- Add synthetic auth smoke checks in EU (owner: SRE)
- Review rate-limiter defaults and add graceful degradation modes (owner: Product)
- Review contract with CacheBridge and add larger SLA + fast-restart runbook (owner: Legal/Procurement)

Ryan (Eng-Infra): acknowledged. Creating Jira EPIC: INF-7421 with the items.

incident-bot: Thread archived as incident-1799943210 when last message posted.
